Thanks — noted. Draft methodology and measurement defs below (summary); full doc attached (redwood_benchmark_methodology_v1.pdf).

Evaluation harness:
- Use redwood-eval v1 (Python) with a reproducible runner config (commit hash included in full doc). The harness emits per-request latency, TTFB (first-chunk time), token counts, and payload sizes.
- Seed: 42 for deterministic sampling and shuffling; provide full script to replay.

Measurement definitions:
- p50/p90/p99: request completion latency (end-to-end) measured from client send to last token received.
- TTFB (streaming): time from client send to the first chunk arrival. We'll also log inter-chunk intervals and average chunk size.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec as observed at server-side, and as observed at client (to capture network effects).
- Warm vs cold: run two phases — (1) cold: 30m idle before the run, single-shot single-client warmup disabled; (2) warm: sustained run after 15m warmup.

Reproducibility:
- We'll publish runner config, seed, prompt-set checksum (sha256), and Docker image tag for the harness.
- Use identical hardware profiles; we'll include GPU/CPU, quantization profile, and model hash.

Resources & timeline:
- Expected runtime for full suite (5K requests, concurrency ramps to 50): ~3-6 hours on one dedicated 8xA100 node. If we include burst/scale tests add 2-3 hours.

Questions for EdgeFin:
- Are we okay to run this on Redwood Hosted or do you require Dedicated / VPC execution? Hosted is faster to turn around; Dedicated gives fully isolated numbers.
- Any additional redlines in the prompt set? We noticed a few system prompts referencing internal taxonomy — please confirm.

Attachment: redwood_benchmark_methodology_v1.pdf
